---
title: Master and RGB curves
description: Shape a clip's contrast, black and white points and colour balance with points on a curve, and reset a channel or every curve.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Curves change the picture's tones with points on a line. Use **Master** for contrast and the black and white points, and **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** to work on one colour at a time. The picture goes through the curves after the [wheels](/color/wheels/) and before the [look](/color/looks/).

<AtAGlance
  keys={['⌫', '⌦', 'Esc', '← → ↑ ↓']}
  where={['Clip inspector ▸ Color ▸ Curves', 'Right-click a channel cell for Reset']}
  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
/>

<Shot
  name="05g-clip-curves.inspector"
  alt="The Curves section open on the Color tab. Six cells read Master, Red, Green, Blue, Hue and Sat, with Master chosen and a dot under Master and Red. Below them a square plot shows a gentle S-curve in black through four points, with the changed Red curve as a faint line behind it. Under the plot are empty In and Out fields and a greyed Delete button."
/>

## The Curves section

Select a video or picture clip, or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/) and open **Curves**. The section starts collapsed, and its header reads "neutral" until a curve changes, then "adjusted".

The section has three parts, from top to bottom:

- The channel picker, which chooses the curve you're editing.
- The plot, a square with a 4 × 4 grid. It grows with the inspector up to 300 pt wide.
- The selected point's **In** and **Out** fields, and **Delete**.

Across the plot is the level going in, from 0 at the left to 1 at the right. Up the plot is the level coming out. A thin diagonal marks a straight curve, which changes nothing.

## The channel picker

Six cells above the plot choose the channel you edit. Click one, and any selected point is deselected.

| Cell | What it changes |
| --- | --- |
| **Master** | All three colours together. Use it for contrast and for the black and white points. |
| **Red** | The red channel only. |
| **Green** | The green channel only. |
| **Blue** | The blue channel only. |
| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue, which turns a chosen hue toward another. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |
| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat, which saturates or mutes a chosen hue. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |

There's no separate luma curve. **Master** runs first, then each colour goes through its own channel, so a **Red** curve works on what **Master** has already done.

The chosen cell is framed and labelled in its channel's colour. A new window starts on **Master**, and the plot stays on your channel while the window is open. The choice isn't saved with the project.

### See which channels are changed

A dot under a cell means that channel has been changed.

Changed channels also show as faint lines in their own colour behind the curve you're editing. **Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** show behind each other, and **Hue** and **Sat** behind each other.

## Shape the picture

| To | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Add contrast | On **Master**, make a gentle S: pull a point low on the curve down, and a point high on the curve up. |
| Set the black point | On **Master**, drag the first point right along the bottom. Everything darker than its **In** comes out black. |
| Set the white point | On **Master**, drag the last point left along the top. Everything brighter than its **In** comes out white. |
| Lift the blacks | On **Master**, drag the first point up the left edge. |
| Warm the shadows | On **Red**, drag the first point up the left edge. |
| Take out a colour cast | On the channel that's too strong, add a point in the middle of the curve and pull it down. |

## Edit points

A curve holds from 2 to 16 points. It runs smoothly through every point and never overshoots, so between two points it stays between their values. Past the first and last points, a tone curve stays flat.

Each of these edits is one undo step, and **Edit ▸ Undo** reads **Undo Curves**.

### Add a point

Click the plot away from any point, or double-click it. Frame Job adds a point on the curve at that position across, wherever you clicked up or down, and selects it. Keep the button down and the same press drags it.

A 17th point beeps, and so does a click with no room left between two points.

On a straight channel, the new point isn't saved until you move it, nudge it or type a value, so a stray click changes nothing. It stays on the plot while it's selected, and it goes when you deselect it or change channel. You can click several in a row to pin a straight curve before you bend it, and they're all saved with the first one you move.

On a channel that already has a shape, the click saves the new point straight away. The picture doesn't change, because the point lies on the curve.

### Drag a point

Press a point within a few points of its square to grab it where it stands, with no jump. It stays inside the plot and just inside its neighbours. The closest it gets to a neighbour across the plot is 0.001 on a tone curve.

You can drag the end points too.

### Fine drag and axis lock

Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag to move the point at a tenth of the speed.

Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> while you drag to lock the point to one axis. It stays put until the pointer has travelled 4 pt from the press, and then whichever direction you moved further wins for the rest of the drag. Let go of <kbd>⇧</kbd> and the point follows the pointer again.

<kbd>⌥</kbd> and <kbd>⇧</kbd> combine.

### Nudge a point

With a point selected, the arrow keys nudge it. Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> to go ten times as far. Each press is one undo step.

| Channel | Arrow key | With <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | 0.01 | 0.1 |
| **Hue** | 1° | 10° |
| **Sat** | 1° across, 0.01 up and down | 10° across, 0.1 up and down |

### In and Out fields

The **In** and **Out** fields below the plot let you type the selected point's position. With no point selected, they're blank and disabled.

| Channel | **In** | **Out** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | 0 to 1, three decimals | 0 to 1, three decimals |
| **Hue** | 0° to 359.9°, one decimal | −180° to +180°, one decimal |
| **Sat** | 0° to 359.9°, one decimal | 0× to 2×, two decimals |

A number outside the range goes to the nearest end of it, and an **In** past a neighbouring point stops just inside that point.

### Delete a point

Select the point and press <kbd>⌫</kbd> or <kbd>⌦</kbd>, choose **Delete** below the plot, or double-click the point.

A curve can't go below two points. The keys and the double-click beep, and **Delete** is greyed out.

### Deselect a point

Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or click another channel. This also hands the keyboard back to the editor.

### The plot and the keyboard

While a point is selected the plot has the keyboard, so:

- The arrow keys nudge the point rather than move the playhead.
- <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point, not the selected clip.

Keys the plot doesn't use still reach the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays.

## Hover readout

While the pointer is over the plot, and during a drag, a small label shows the pointer's position and the curve's value there.

| Channel | The label reads |
| --- | --- |
| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | `In 0.42 → Out 0.47` |
| **Hue** | `Hue 34° → +12°` |
| **Sat** | `Hue 120° → ×0.80` |

There's no label outside the plot, and that includes the spectrum strip under a hue channel.

## Reset curves

To straighten one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Master**, **Reset Red**, **Reset Green**, **Reset Blue**, **Reset Hue** or **Reset Sat**. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.

To straighten all six channels, choose **Reset** in the section's header. It shows while a curve is changed, and it's one undo step. You can also right-click the plot and choose **Reset to default**.

## Curves inside an action

With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a curve edit goes to the action's end, so the curve animates. Any two curves animate into each other, whatever their number of points, and so does a curve and a straight line.

The plot shows it in its own way: the action's start curve is dashed, and the edited curve and its points are in the action colour.

To animate a curve back to neutral, right-click a cell and choose its **Reset** item, or right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**. Each writes a straight curve to the action's end, for the channels that aren't already straight. The section's **Reset** isn't there while the action is selected. **Clear** takes its place once the action animates curves, and removes them from the action.

See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

## Good to know

With several clips selected, the plot shows the first clip's curves, and the row shows **mixed** when they differ. An edit gives every selected clip the curve you're editing, for that channel, and leaves their other channels alone.

Selecting another clip deselects the point.

## With an agent

An agent writes a whole channel at once as a list of points, and that list replaces the channel. Where a drag stops at a limit, Frame Job turns down an agent's value outside the limits rather than moving it to the nearest one. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/)
- [Wheels](/color/wheels/)
- [Looks](/color/looks/)
- [Waveform and RGB Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/)
- [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/)

---
title: Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves
description: Turn one colour toward another, or saturate or mute it, without touching the rest of the picture.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The hue curves work on one colour at a time. **Hue** turns a chosen hue toward another, such as making the greens more teal. **Sat** saturates or mutes a chosen hue, such as calming a loud red. Both leave the other colours alone.

<AtAGlance
  where="Clip inspector ▸ Color ▸ Curves ▸ the Hue and Sat cells"
  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
/>

## The two hue channels

The **Hue** and **Sat** cells in the channel picker put the plot into degrees. Each channel lays the colours out across the plot, and its height says what happens to the colour at that position.

| Cell | Curve | Across | Up | The centre line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue | Hue, 0° to 360° | A shift, −180° to +180° | 0°, no shift |
| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat | Hue, 0° to 360° | A gain, 0× to 2× | 1×, unchanged |

So a straight hue channel is a flat line across the middle, not a diagonal. It starts with two points on that line, at 0° and 180°.

Points work as they do on any curve: click to add one, drag, nudge, type, delete and reset. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/#edit-points). A channel holds 2 to 16 points.

The hue curves run after **Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** and before the [look](/color/looks/), so they read each colour as those curves left it. Both hue curves read that colour once, before either changes it. A **Sat** point on the greens still acts on greens you've turned teal with **Hue**.

## The spectrum strip

A strip under the plot shows which colour each position stands for, from 0° at the left to 360° at the right. Thin lines mark every 60°, with lines across at the quarters and a stronger line at the centre.

| Hue | Colour |
| --- | --- |
| 0° | Red |
| 60° | Yellow |
| 120° | Green |
| 180° | Cyan |
| 240° | Blue |
| 300° | Magenta |

## Hue vs Hue

A positive shift moves a colour to the right along the strip, from red toward yellow and green. A negative shift moves it to the left. Brightness stays as it was.

To make the greens more teal:

<Steps>

1. Select the clip, open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), open **Curves** and click the **Hue** cell.

2. Click the plot at about 90° and again at about 150°, without dragging. These two points hold the colours either side still.

3. Press the plot at about 120° and drag up. The label reads `Hue 120° → +30°` and so on as you go.

</Steps>

The outer points are saved with the first point you move. Without them, the shift spreads as far as the points at 0° and 180°.

## Hue vs Sat

Above the centre line a hue gets more saturated, and below it less. At the bottom of the plot, 0×, that hue goes grey. At the top, 2×, its saturation doubles. Saturation scales around the colour's own brightness.

To mute the reds:

<Steps>

1. Click the **Sat** cell.

2. Click the plot at about 330° and again at about 30°, without dragging. A click at a point's position selects that point instead, so keep clear of the point at 0°.

3. Drag the point at 0° down. The label reads `Hue 0° → ×0.60` and so on as you go.

</Steps>

## Hue curve safeguards

- **A grey stays grey.** A grey has no real hue to read, so a hue curve never tints it. When a colour's strongest and weakest channels are within 2% of each other it's left alone, and the effect fades in to full strength at 6%.
- **Points never cross the wrap.** A point stops at 0° and 359.9°, so it can't slide round to the other end. The curve itself does wrap: its right end runs on smoothly into its left end, so a shift around red covers both ends of the plot.
- **Colours stay in range.** When a turned colour can't keep its brightness, it gives up some saturation rather than clip.

## Good to know

- The closest a point gets to a neighbour across the plot is 0.1°.
- **Reset Hue** and **Reset Sat** straighten one channel from the cell's right-click menu. The section's **Reset** straightens all six, the tone curves included. See [Reset curves](/color/curves/#reset-curves).
- The **Hue** slider in the [Color section](/color/color-section/) turns every colour at once. Hue vs Hue turns only the colours you choose.
- Hue curves animate inside an action as tone curves do. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).

## With an agent

An agent writes each hue curve whole, as a list of hue and value pairs, and that list replaces the channel. It can place a point anywhere from 0 up to, but not including, 360. A value outside the limits is turned down, not moved to the nearest one. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).

## Related

- [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/)
- [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/)
- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
- [Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue](/color/color-section/)

Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

import json
import re
import sys

ROOT = "/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/src/content/docs/color/"
SCRATCH = "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kevingalligan-devel-framejob/9cfd7405-83ec-4caa-905f-7b97a20f2cc9/scratchpad/inventory/"

EDITS = {
    "curves.mdx": [
        (
            "Press a point within a few points of its square to grab it where it stands, with no jump. "
            "It stays inside the plot and just inside its neighbours. The closest it gets to a neighbour "
            "across the plot is 0.001 on a tone curve.",
            "Press a point to grab it where it stands, with no jump, and drag. It stays inside the plot "
            "and can't pass its neighbours. The closest it gets to a neighbour across the plot is 0.001 "
            "on a tone curve.",
        ),
        (
            "an **In** past a neighbouring point stops just inside that point.",
            "an **In** past a neighbouring point stops short of that point.",
        ),
        (
            "Each of these edits is one undo step, and **Edit ▸ Undo** reads **Undo Curves**.",
            "Each drag, nudge, deletion or typed value is one undo step, and **Edit ▸ Undo** reads "
            "**Undo Curves**.",
        ),
    ],
    "hue-curves.mdx": [
        (
            "3. Press the plot at about 120° and drag up. The label reads `Hue 120° → +30°` and so on as you go.",
            "3. Press the centre line at about 120° and drag up. The label reads `Hue 120° → +30°` and so on as you go.",
        ),
        (
            "2. Click the plot at about 330° and again at about 30°, without dragging. A click at a point's "
            "position selects that point instead, so keep clear of the point at 0°.",
            "2. Click the plot at about 330° and again at about 30°, without dragging. These two points "
            "hold the colours either side still.",
        ),
        (
            "3. Drag the point at 0° down.",
            "3. Drag the point at 0°, at the left end of the centre line, down.",
        ),
    ],
}

for name, edits in EDITS.items():
    path = ROOT + name
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    for old, new in edits:
        if text.count(old) != 1:
            sys.exit(f"{name}: not exactly once: {old[:50]}")
        text = text.replace(old, new)
    open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text)

ANCHORS = {
    "color-curves-section": "the-curves-section",
    "color-curve-picker": "the-channel-picker",
    "color-curve-master": "the-channel-picker",
    "color-curve-red": "the-channel-picker",
    "color-curve-green": "the-channel-picker",
    "color-curve-blue": "the-channel-picker",
    "color-curve-siblings": "see-which-channels-are-changed",
    "color-curve-dot": "see-which-channels-are-changed",
    "color-curve-point-limits": "edit-points",
    "color-curve-add-point": "add-a-point",
    "color-curve-unsaved-point": "add-a-point",
    "color-curve-drag-point": "drag-a-point",
    "color-curve-fine-drag": "fine-drag-and-axis-lock",
    "color-curve-axis-lock": "fine-drag-and-axis-lock",
    "color-curve-nudge": "nudge-a-point",
    "color-curve-delete-point": "delete-a-point",
    "color-curve-deselect": "deselect-a-point",
    "color-curve-keyboard": "the-plot-and-the-keyboard",
    "color-curve-fields": "in-and-out-fields",
    "color-curve-hover-readout": "hover-readout",
    "color-curve-undo": "edit-points",
    "color-curve-reset-channel": "reset-curves",
    "color-curve-reset-all": "reset-curves",
    "color-curves-by-agent": "with-an-agent",
    "color-hue-curves": "the-two-hue-channels",
    "color-curve-hue-hue": "hue-vs-hue",
    "color-curve-hue-sat": "hue-vs-sat",
    "color-hue-plot-strip": "the-spectrum-strip",
    "color-hue-curve-safeguards": "hue-curve-safeguards",
    "color-hue-curves-by-agent": "with-an-agent",
}

brief = json.load(open(SCRATCH + "chunks/color-3.json", encoding="utf-8"))
ids = [(p["slug"], f["id"]) for p in brief["pages"] for f in p["features"]]
assert {i for _, i in ids} == set(ANCHORS), set(i for _, i in ids) ^ set(ANCHORS)


def slug(heading):
    heading = heading.strip().lower().replace("`", "")
    heading = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", heading)
    return heading.replace(" ", "-")


for page, fid in ids:
    text = open(ROOT + page.split("/")[1] + ".mdx", encoding="utf-8").read()
    found = {slug(m) for m in re.findall(r"^#{2,4} (.+)$", text, re.M)}
    assert ANCHORS[fid] in found, (fid, ANCHORS[fid])

json.dump(ANCHORS, open(SCRATCH + "anchors/color-3.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=1)
print(len(ANCHORS), "anchors")
